friction_layers.title: Marcus Aurelius and Stoic Virtue
friction_layers.observation: Humans recognize the need for virtue, discipline, and self-control.
friction_layers.pattern: Character shapes the direction of the soul and life.
friction_layers.friction_point: Human beings often recognize virtue but fail to fully live by it.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Stoicism emphasizes reason, discipline, acceptance, and virtue.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes grace, redemption through Christ, and transformation by the Holy Spirit.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Human reason can recognize moral order, but restoration after failure requires a deeper resolution.

friction_layers.title: Epictetus and Agency Under Limits
friction_layers.observation: Humans experience a real difference between what they can control and what they cannot control.
friction_layers.pattern: Moral agency grows when a person learns responsibility without pretending to control all outcomes.
friction_layers.friction_point: Acceptance can become wisdom, but it can also become resignation when suffering or injustice should be resisted.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Stoicism emphasizes disciplined judgment, inner freedom, and acceptance of what lies beyond personal control.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes faithful agency before God, prayerful dependence, patient endurance, and justice-seeking love.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Human agency is real but finite; the deeper resolution joins responsibility with dependence on grace and hope beyond visible control.

friction_layers.title: Plato and the Ordered Soul
friction_layers.observation: Humans recognize that justice requires order within the person and the community.
friction_layers.pattern: The shape of the soul affects the shape of public life.
friction_layers.friction_point: A vision of order can become coercive when it ranks people by function, knowledge, or social usefulness.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Plato emphasizes philosophical reason, education, hierarchy, and the ordering of desire toward the good.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes created dignity, servant leadership, repentance, grace, and justice for vulnerable people.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Reason can perceive that the soul and society need order, but Christian resolution tests order by love, humility, and the dignity of every person.

friction_layers.title: Aristotle and Virtue Formation
friction_layers.observation: Humans become shaped by repeated habits, practices, loves, and communities.
friction_layers.pattern: Formation turns moral insight into embodied character.
friction_layers.friction_point: Virtue can be treated as achievement, social polish, or excellence without grace for failure and repair.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Aristotle emphasizes habit, practical wisdom, moderation, friendship, and the cultivation of excellence.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes spiritual formation, grace, repentance, sanctification, and love that is not limited to the socially excellent.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Habit matters deeply, but Christian transformation requires more than training; it requires grace that reforms desire and restores failed persons.

friction_layers.title: Kant and Moral Duty
friction_layers.observation: Humans recognize a moral law that calls them beyond preference, appetite, and convenience.
friction_layers.pattern: Duty reveals that moral life has a claim on the self.
friction_layers.friction_point: Moral duty can identify obligation without healing the divided will or restoring the person after failure.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Kant emphasizes reason, duty, autonomy, and acting according to moral law rather than inclination.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes moral accountability together with grace, forgiveness, union with Christ, and transformation by the Holy Spirit.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Moral law can expose responsibility, but the deeper resolution must address guilt, weakness, forgiveness, and renewal.
sources: Immanuel Kant, Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals

friction_layers.title: Nietzsche and the Critique of Moral Weakness
friction_layers.observation: Humans can use moral language to hide fear, resentment, domination, or weakness.
friction_layers.pattern: Moral claims must be tested by what they produce in real character and community.
friction_layers.friction_point: Christian language can be misused as a mask for passivity, control, or resentment rather than cruciform love.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Nietzsche emphasizes strength, self-overcoming, suspicion of herd morality, and the creation of values.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity emphasizes the cross as power made humble, repentance from false righteousness, and Spirit-formed love that is neither domination nor resentment.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: A serious critique of moral hypocrisy can purify the pattern by forcing Christian claims to show truthful humility, courage, mercy, and costly love.
sources: Friedrich Nietzsche, On the Genealogy of Morality

friction_layers.title: Hume and Moral Sentiment
friction_layers.observation: Humans often make moral judgments through sympathy, feeling, habit, and social experience rather than pure reason alone.
friction_layers.pattern: Moral perception involves the whole person, not detached intellect only.
friction_layers.friction_point: If morality is grounded only in sentiment, it can struggle to name an authority beyond preference, culture, or shared feeling.
friction_layers.non_christian_resolution: Hume emphasizes sympathy, custom, moral sentiment, and the limits of reason in human judgment.
friction_layers.christian_resolution: Christianity affirms embodied moral perception while grounding goodness in God's character, revelation, love, and the formation of rightly ordered desire.
friction_layers.divine_pattern_insight: Moral feeling is a real part of human response, but the deeper resolution asks how desire is healed, trained, and accountable to truth.
sources: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals
